description.summary: lay a window out at a named place in the desktop

protocol.description:
Domicile draws the desktop as a web page, and each window as an element in it. This protocol lets a client ask for its window to be laid out at a named place in that page, an anchor, such as a slot in a panel, rather than placed as an ordinary window.
The page lays the window out with its own elements, so the window moves with them in the same frame. Its size still comes from xdg_toplevel's configure, set from the box the page gives it.
What anchors exist, and what each name means, is up to the desktop. A desktop with no anchor of the name asked for treats the window as an ordinary one.

interface.name: domicile_anchor_manager_v1
interface.description: The global that hands out a window's anchor object.

entry.name: already_anchored
entry.summary: the toplevel already has an anchor object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Anchor objects already made keep working.

request.name: get_toplevel_anchor

description.summary: the anchor object of a window

request.description: Make the object that sets toplevel's anchor. A toplevel has at most one; asking for a second while the first exists is the already_anchored error.

interface.name: domicile_toplevel_anchor_v1
interface.description: Sets the anchor of one toplevel. A window has no anchor until it sets one.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The window has no anchor from its surface's next commit.

request.name: set_anchor

description.summary: name the anchor to lay the window out at

request.description: Ask for the window to be laid out at the anchor called name, or at none for null. Double-buffered: applied on the surface's next wl_surface.commit. Set before the window's first buffer is committed, the window first appears at its anchor.
